name: Hear It Before You See It
why_it_works: Taking away the picture makes people listen harder to the client's real track, and the imagination fills the gap with its own image. When the cover art finally sharpens, it either matches what they pictured or surprises them, and both feel like a payoff.

hook.pattern: Black screen, sound first, and a line telling the viewer to turn the sound on before the art appears.
examples: Sound on. You hear it before you see it.
Close your eyes for ten seconds. Then look.

variables.name: artist_name
variables.description: Artist, label, show or team name

variables.name: release_title
variables.description: Name of the single, mix or episode, 4 words or fewer

variables.name: sound_words
variables.description: Three words that describe the sound, starts with a capital letter

variables.name: audio_clip
variables.description: The client's own released audio (owned or licensed), the 15-20 seconds with the clearest drop or change
variables.example: the second chorus of Low Tide, 0:58 to 1:16

beats.purpose: hook: sound before picture; {{audio_clip}} starts here and runs under the whole reel

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 almost black frame, a single thin glowing line in the center like a quiet audio waveform, deep shadow, subtle film grain
Abstract slow-moving light ribbons pulsing in deep blue and amber on black, smoke-like texture, vertical 9:16, no people, no text
The {{release_title}} cover art heavily blurred, only colors and a rough shape visible, vignette, vertical 9:16
The same {{release_title}} cover art lightly blurred, main shape now clear, same framing, vertical 9:16

beats.purpose: the reveal: art in focus, timed to the drop in the real track

visual.prompt: The {{release_title}} cover art snapping into sharp focus with a slow parallax push-in and soft light sweep, vertical 9:16

craft.notes: Use the client's own track, not generated music: lay {{audio_clip}} under the whole reel and keep the screen nearly dark for the first half. Rack the art from blur to focus in steps, timed to the drop, so the eyes catch up to the ears.

do_not: Use any audio the client does not own or license, or swap in generated music; the real track is the point
Imitate a named artist's sound, voice or cover style
Put lyrics on screen that are not the artist's own
Choose a part of the track without a clear drop or change for the reveal to land on
compliance: Audio: the client must own or license the track, episode clip or mix used; keep the license or release record on file
No real artist's likeness, lyrics, melody or sound-alike other than the client's own work
Label the generated abstract visuals as AI-generated where the platform requires it
